title: The Digital Revolution: Layers and Inclusion
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
The digital revolution has no single birthday. Transistors and integrated circuits made electronic computation smaller, cheaper, and more reliable. Software made the same hardware perform many tasks. Packet-switched networks allowed distant computers to exchange data. Each layer depended on earlier research, manufacturing, standards, and institutions; invention was cumulative rather than solitary.

The Internet and the World Wide Web are related but not identical. The Internet is a network of networks that carries data through shared protocols. The Web is one service built on that infrastructure, using linked documents, addresses, and transfer rules. It was proposed at CERN in 1989 to help researchers share information, and CERN's decision to release the software openly in 1993 supported wider adoption. Openness lowered barriers, but browsers, servers, cables, firms, and users still had to develop.

Once many people joined, network effects changed value: a communication system became more useful as potential partners increased. The same mechanism could also favor large platforms that accumulated users and data. Digital services reduced search and communication costs, enabled new forms of work and science, and improved access to some services. They also created risks involving privacy, cybersecurity, misinformation, market power, and dependence on systems that users cannot inspect.

“Access” therefore has several levels. A network may reach a region while devices or data remain unaffordable. A person may be connected but lack skills, accessible design, a secure identity, or meaningful local content. Digital inclusion is not achieved by counting cables alone. Evaluation must ask who can use a system safely, for what purpose, under whose rules, and with what route to challenge an error.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: The Web and the Internet were invented at the same moment by one person.

options.label: B
options.text: Physical network coverage alone guarantees equal digital participation.

options.label: C
options.text: Layered technologies and institutions expanded digital capabilities while creating benefits, risks, and unequal forms of access.

options.label: D
options.text: Network effects always prevent large platforms from gaining power.

questions.answer: 正解：C。本文は技術と制度の累積、ネットワーク効果、便益とリスク、アクセスの多層性を結び付けます。A・B・Dは本文が明確に否定する単純化です。

questions.prompt: Why does the author say that the digital revolution has “no single birthday”?

options.label: A
options.text: Its capabilities accumulated through multiple technological and institutional layers over time.

options.label: B
options.text: No dates are known for transistors, networks, or the Web.

options.label: C
options.text: All digital technologies appeared simultaneously in 1993.

options.label: D
options.text: Software developed without relying on hardware or earlier research.

questions.answer: 正解：A。計算部品、ソフトウェア、ネットワークなどが先行研究・製造・標準・制度に依存して積み重なったためです。B～Dは年代や相互依存について本文と矛盾します。

questions.prompt: The phrase “cumulative rather than solitary” in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: built by combining many earlier contributions rather than created in isolation

options.label: B
options.text: produced secretly by one institution without standards

options.label: C
options.text: limited to a single invention that replaced all earlier work

options.label: D
options.text: independent of manufacturing and research

questions.answer: 正解：A。cumulativeは先行する多数の貢献が蓄積すること、solitaryは孤立した単独発明を指します。B～Dは累積性と依存関係を逆転させます。

questions.prompt: How does the passage distinguish the Internet from the World Wide Web?

options.label: A
options.text: The Internet is the network infrastructure using shared protocols, whereas the Web is a linked-document service built on it.

options.label: B
options.text: The Web carries all data, whereas the Internet is only a collection of documents.

options.label: C
options.text: They are two names for an identical invention released in 1989.

options.label: D
options.text: The Internet depends on the Web, but the Web requires no network infrastructure.

questions.answer: 正解：A。Internetは共有プロトコルでデータを運ぶネットワーク基盤、Webはその上の文書・アドレス・転送規則を使うサービスです。B～Dは基盤とサービスの関係を誤ります。

questions.prompt: Why was releasing the Web software openly not sufficient by itself for widespread adoption?

options.label: A
options.text: Complementary browsers, servers, cables, firms, and users still had to develop.

options.label: B
options.text: Open release made shared protocols impossible to use.

options.label: C
options.text: The Web could function without computers, networks, or users.

options.label: D
options.text: CERN prohibited other organizations from developing related tools.

questions.answer: 正解：A。公開は障壁を下げましたが、利用を可能にするブラウザ、サーバー、回線、企業、利用者という補完要素も必要でした。B～Dは本文の因果関係と逆です。

questions.prompt: What two effects of network effects does the passage identify?

options.label: A
options.text: They can increase a system's usefulness as participation grows and can also strengthen platforms that accumulate users and data.

options.label: B
options.text: They reduce usefulness as users join and always divide markets equally.

options.label: C
options.text: They eliminate privacy risks and make platform size irrelevant.

options.label: D
options.text: They affect cables only and have no relationship to communication value.

questions.answer: 正解：A。参加相手が増えると価値が高まる一方、利用者とデータを蓄積する大規模プラットフォームを有利にもします。B～Dは価値増加と集中の両面を捉えていません。

questions.prompt: Why does physical network access not necessarily amount to digital inclusion?

options.label: A
options.text: People may still face unaffordable devices or data, limited skills, inaccessible design, insecure identity, or a lack of meaningful local content.

options.label: B
options.text: A cable automatically supplies every user with skills and affordable devices.

options.label: C
options.text: Inclusion concerns only the number of servers in a region.

options.label: D
options.text: Connected people never need a way to appeal an error.

questions.answer: 正解：A。本文は費用、技能、アクセシビリティ、安全な本人確認、地域に意味のある内容を別のアクセス層として挙げます。B～Dはアクセスを物理接続だけに縮小します。

questions.prompt: What does the final sentence suggest should be examined when evaluating a digital system?

options.label: A
options.text: Who can use it, for which purposes, under whose governance, and how errors can be challenged

options.label: B
options.text: Only the total length of cables installed

options.label: C
options.text: Only whether the service attracts the largest possible platform

options.label: D
options.text: Whether users can be prevented from questioning automated decisions

questions.answer: 正解：A。最終文は利用者の分布、利用目的、統治規則、誤りへの異議申立てを評価軸にします。B～Dは本文が批判する狭い評価や説明責任の欠如です。

questions.prompt: Which evaluation plan best reflects the passage's concept of digital inclusion?

options.label: A
options.text: Test representative users and measure cost, task completion, errors, security, time, help needs, abandonment, data use, appeal routes, and offline alternatives.

options.label: B
options.text: Count network cables and assume every connected person can participate safely.

options.label: C
options.text: Measure only total sign-ups and ignore who abandons the service or why.

options.label: D
options.text: Exclude users who need accessible design so that testing is faster.

questions.answer: 正解：A。代表的利用者で費用・達成度・誤り・安全・支援・離脱・データ利用・異議申立て・代替手段まで測る案が多層的アクセスを検証します。B～Dは公平性と実利用を見落とします。
